Born about 1720, at Salem by the tree and in Essex County by the family book, son of Thomas Hutchins,
who had come over from Dorset, and Sarah Southwick.
In 1730 his father moved the family inland from Salem to Dudley, in Worcester County.
At Dudley’s town meeting of 1 March 1742 the town chose "thomas hutchens jur" hog reeve for the west end of the town,
and in February 1744 he married Abigail Pierce (Perce) of Dudley at Oxford.
Their son Thomas was born at Dudley in 1747.
The family book says that he, the eldest son, moved on to Winchester, New Hampshire,
and raised there a large family that spread through New Hampshire and Vermont, and its 1984 sequel has him dying at
Winchester. Abigail lived to 97 and died at Oxford in 1818.
